$comment: Riftlight authored opening draft. Development preview only; see ../README.md. Production campaign id will be riftlight. No bonus XP: preserve the design bible campaign budget.
title: Land Under an Unfamiliar Sky

goal.text: Find your feet on an island high in the sky.

steps.label: Learn to listen for a rift
Help the keeper guard the edge
Find which way the song leads

plate.narration: High above the realm, stone islands drift like slow boats. Gold-roofed temples glow on their backs. Roots dangle into the clouds, and wind banners snap in every direction at once.

island.narration: The fold opens onto cold stone high above the realm, then shuts behind you with a pop. A kitsune temple keeper hooks an arm through a rope ring. "Hold on! These are called the Sky Islands, and this one is not where it belongs." Your job: find your feet up here. Learn to hear the rift, help guard the edge, and find where the singing leads.

variants.text: The Cairnstep griffins set your party down on a stone pad high above the realm, then are gone in three flaps. A kitsune temple keeper hooks an arm through a rope ring. "Hold on! These are called the Sky Islands. Our old landing route points into empty sky now." Your job: find your feet up here. Learn to hear the rift, help guard the edge, and find where the singing leads.

landing.prompt: The wind slams the landing pad like a door. "Grab a rope ring and hold on!" shouts the keeper.

landing_held.narration: Every hand finds a ring, and the gust howls past. "Good grips," says the keeper. "Most visitors arrive sitting down." She leads you past a gold-roofed shrine with a bronze bell as big as a barrel, and hands you a wrapped supper bundle. "Eat when the wind lets you."

landing_slid.narration: The wind scoops you off your feet, and you slide across the boards like soap. The keeper's rope hooks the last boot near the edge. Your hats keep going. One lands on a gull, which now looks very official. She leads you past a gold-roofed shrine with a bronze bell and gives you a supper bundle for the scrapes.

lesson.narration: Seren Wisp, the kitsune from the glacier, is comparing notes with a young manticore named Pip Thistledown. "I count what has moved," says Pip, tapping his notebook. "The count keeps changing. Help me listen." Seren asks you to hum the hall note and listen for an answer. "A starweaver can learn to answer a rift's hum. That is called Attune."

variants.text: Seren Wisp and Pip Thistledown are here too, checking another moved route. "The count keeps changing here too," says Pip. "Help me listen." Seren asks you to compare the sounds with what she taught you before.

pip_notes.narration: Pip's notebook is full of tiny islands and crossed-out arrows. "This one was east of here at breakfast. Now it is south. Rude." He taps a smudge. "When a sound out there moves, the islands near it move too. I think. Will you help me listen?"

hum.prompt: Hum the hall note, then listen hard. Where does the answering sound come from?

hum_attuned.prompt: Hum back to the rift with Attune, and find where its answer comes from.

hum_heard.narration: A thin hum answers from the east, then again from the very same spot. Seren's ears swing up. "That is a rift. Its hum stays put while the wind runs around. A hum is steady. Wind is a liar." Pip writes EAST and underlines it twice, in case east moves.

hum_fuzzy.narration: The wind swallows your note. Seren has you press a palm flat to the stone instead. There it is, low and steady, a hum in your hand. Pip writes EAST with a question mark, and gives the question mark a tiny hat.

local.narration: The keeper shows you a rope between two marker posts. Yesterday it pointed to the next island. Now it points at empty sky. "And travelers keep following it," she sighs. A low song drifts in from beyond the mist. How will you keep travelers back from the edge?

markers.narration: The keeper has three cairn stones on wooden sleds, each stone as heavy as a sleeping goat. They belong on the path, where travelers will see them. The boards are slick with mist, and the wind keeps trying to help.

markers_check.prompt: Drag the cairn sleds along the slick path, and keep them straight.

markers_set.narration: Three cairns stand in a line, tall enough to see in fog. The keeper strings a warning cord between them. It hums. "One less traveler walking toward an old view." Pip salutes the nearest cairn, in case it is somebody important.

markers_dropped.narration: The last stone slides off its sled and drops over the edge. You wait for a crash. None comes. "It will land somewhere," says the keeper. She ties her washing line between the two cairns you saved and clips a spoon to it. The spoon clatters a fine warning.

song.narration: You wait for the low song again. It comes from somewhere the keeper did not expect. She hands you her slate and chalk. "Point at it every time it sounds. If most of you agree, we have a true bearing."

song_check.prompt: Point at the song each time it sounds, so the keeper can chalk a true bearing.

song_bearing.narration: Most fingers point the same way: east, and a little down. The keeper chalks a bold line, then the old route beside it. They do not match at all. "The song has moved," she says. "So have we." She moves the marker posts to your line. Her scarf, tied on top, flaps east.

song_muddled.narration: Fingers point east, south, and one straight up at a gull. The slate looks like a spider fell in the chalk. "The song bounces off the mist," says the keeper kindly. She picks east and moves the marker posts. The gull looks insulted.

edge_scout.prompt: Fly out over the edge, and hold steady in the gusts long enough to see the whole island.

edge_scouted.narration: From up here the island looks like a dropped cookie: a shrine, a landing pad, a pole with an iron basket, and a rope road to nowhere. Far off, a long shape slides through the mist, singing. You land and draw the keeper a map. She nods so hard her ears flap.

edge_gusted.narration: A gust spins you like a leaf and drops you back on the pad. But you saw enough: the edge is longer than the rope. You help the keeper drag three cairns to the spots you remember. They lean a little, like friends telling a secret.

walker.narration: A rattle comes down the old rope road. A kite seller is pulling a cart toward the edge, nose in a map. The map is upside down. The road ends in empty air twenty steps ahead. "Dob! Stop!" shouts the keeper. He waves and keeps walking. How will you stop him?

walker_catch.prompt: Sprint down the slick boards, and catch the cart rope before the wheel reaches the last plank.

walker_call.prompt: Wave the warning cord and call his name, loud and kind, until he looks up.

walker_leap.prompt: Leap over the cart onto the last plank, land square and turn the cart around.

walker_safe.narration: Dob stops, one wheel on the last plank. He looks down. He turns his map right side up. "Ah. The road went wrong. I did not." He sells kites to the next island. "You saved my cart," he says, and hands you a bundle of bright kite-flags. "Wave these, and the whole sky will see." He ties a springy lace on your ankle, for quick feet, and counts four coins into your hand.

walker_dragged.narration: The cart tips at the last plank, one wheel in the sky. You haul it back while kites spill off like startled birds. Dob dangles from his strap, smiling. "Ah. Wrong road." Safe on stone, he hands you a bundle of bright kite-flags. "Wave these, and the whole sky will see." He finds three coins in his pockets for you.

edge_merge.narration: The keeper points to a tall pole with an iron basket on top. "The signal basket. At dusk we light it, so islands and ferries can find us. The pole is crooked from the move, and our fuel is a mess. A ferry captain named Thimble is due tonight. Without a light, she will never find us."

basket_plan.narration: The pole leans like a sleepy giraffe, its stone foot cracked loose. "If that tips at dusk," says Pip, chewing his pencil, "the fire goes over the edge." The keeper hands you rope and a pile of wedge stones. How will you set it straight before dark?

pole_ropes.prompt: Loop the ropes around the pole and heave together on the keeper's count!

pole_wedge.prompt: Find which wedge stones fit the cracked foot, and in what order.

pole_smash.prompt: Smash the pole upright, then seat its foot without cracking it again.

pole_brace.prompt: Brace the foot steady while friends tie off the ropes.

pole_up.narration: The pole stands as straight as a spoon in porridge. The keeper taps the basket, and it rings, proud and tinny. Pip held one rope a moment too long and got lifted off the ground. Nobody mentions it, loudly.

pole_leaning.narration: The pole stands, mostly. It leans a thumb's width east and creaks at every gust. The keeper ties on two more ropes and gives it a stern look. "It will hold. It just has opinions."

fuel.narration: "No fire without fuel," sighs the keeper. Her oil jars cracked in the move. The woodshed under the shrine holds dry logs, if you can carry them across the windy yard. The orchard has windfall twigs, if you can catch them first. What will you fetch?

fuel_logs.prompt: Carry the dry logs across the yard while the wind shoves at every armful.

fuel_twigs.prompt: Chase the windfall twigs before the wind blows them over the edge!

fuel_lace.prompt: Your springy lace makes your feet light. Race the gusts to the dry logs and back.

fuel_dash.prompt: Dash to the dry logs before the next gust, and get every armful back.

fuel_dry.narration: You stack the fuel at the foot of the pole. Dry wood smells like a warm kitchen, even in a gale. Pip carries the last twig, the size of a pencil, like a sword.

fuel_soggy.narration: Half the wood is wet, and the other half is wetter. "This will burn," says the keeper. "It will not like it." She slips you a bundle of shrine incense to help. "Do not tell the shrine," she whispers.

light.narration: The sun sinks behind the mist. The basket is full, and someone must light it in a gale. The keeper holds out a flint striker and a clay pot of shrine coals. Seren licks a finger and checks the wind. "Fast and bright, or slow and careful. Either works, if nobody sneezes."

light_flint.prompt: Strike the flint while everyone cups hands and cloaks around the sparks.

light_coals.prompt: Pass the pot of coals hand to hand up the ladder, slow and steady.

light_fox.prompt: Coax your fox fire into the wood, and make it hold when the pole sways.

basket_lit.narration: The flame catches and stands up tall and gold. Far off in the mist, a tiny light blinks back. "There," says the keeper. "Now the sky can find us." Pip bows to the basket. The keeper hands you a brass whistle from the shrine. "One loud note, for when the sky must hear you."

basket_smoky.narration: The wood sulks, smokes, and gives a small flame that coughs at every gust. The keeper feeds it shrine incense, and it brightens to a wobbly glow that smells like lemon cake. It will be seen. Just not smoothly.

dusk_ferry.narration: A griffin drops out of the dusk onto the pole rail, satchel flapping. "Fenwick, courier! Every island has been hunting for your light. Captain Thimble's ferry is right behind me, and the wind is swinging her sideways. She needs a landing now!" How will you bring her in?

variants.text: "The Cairnstep watchers told me where you landed," he adds. "They said to look after you."

ferry_lines.prompt: Snatch the trailing lines as they whip past, and loop them around the mooring posts.

ferry_flags.prompt: Read the ferry's heading through the mist, and wave the kite-flags: left, right, hold.

ferry_tow.prompt: Fly out over the gap, catch the line and pull the ferry straight.

ferry_whistle.prompt: Blow one loud note, again and again, so the ferry can steer straight to the sound.

ferry_post.prompt: Brace the mooring post while friends haul the ferry in, hand over hand.

ferry_in.narration: The ferry thumps against the pad and stays. Hens flap out of a basket and strut about. A kitsune steps off, her captain's hat tied on with string. "Captain Thimble. Best landing all week." Her passengers cling to the rail and will not let go. "I need a safe lane home for them," she says, "and a very strong cup of tea."

variants.text: Then she stares. "You! From the Exchange quay! You found us. See? Same washing." A line of damp socks flaps from the rail.

ferry_bumped.narration: The ferry bumps the pad and bounces off like a ball. A crate of washing spills socks everywhere. Hens flap out and strut about. A kitsune steps off, her captain's hat tied on with string. "Captain Thimble. I have had worse landings. Not this week." Her passengers cling to the rail. "I need a safe lane home for them, and a very strong cup of tea."

variants.text: Then she stares. "You! From the Exchange quay! You found us. See? Same washing." She waves a sock at you.

passengers.narration: The ferry is tied up, but the passengers still cling to the rail. The keeper brings a ladder and a blanket. How will you help them down?

passengers_fed.narration: You pass the supper around. One by one, the passengers let go of the rail to hold some bread. The keeper sends them to the shrine for barley tea, and the hens follow in a line. Thimble flops onto a barrel.

passengers_calm.narration: You speak softly and offer a steady hand. One by one, the passengers step onto firm stone. The keeper sends them off for barley tea. The hens follow in a line, as if they planned it. Thimble flops onto a barrel.

passengers_stuck.narration: The keeper brings rice crackers, and nobody hurries. The passengers climb down one crunch at a time. Thimble sits on a barrel and watches the hens follow them. "Next time," she says, "I bring only hens."

thimble.narration: Thimble unrolls a chart and holds it flat with three hens. "My old lane is gone. I steered by the cloud whales' song. Where they sing, the sky stays level. Now the song has wandered." The ferry rail hums faintly, leaning east. Fenwick's feather leans east too. "Find where the song comes from," says Thimble, "and Fenwick will tell every island."

windbreak_rest.narration: The keeper builds a wind wall of baskets and blankets. Hot barley tea goes around in chipped cups. The hens roost on Pip, who bears it nobly. Dob hangs his kites along the wall and opens his ribbon cart. Far off, the low song comes again.

pip_night.narration: Pip's notebook is soaked at one corner. You dry the pages by the fire while he reads his list aloud: islands that moved, three socks, a hen named Gravy. "I don't know why it all moves," he says quietly. "Counting is easier with friends." Gravy agrees, from his head.

night_song.narration: Night. The sky is huge and full of stars. The shrine bell shivers all by itself. Then the low song comes, close and slow, rolling over the island like a wave. "That is the nearest it has been," says the keeper. "Tonight we find which way it leads."

bearing_vote.narration: Everyone has a clue: the hum you heard this morning, the keeper's chalk slate, Thimble's humming rail, Fenwick's feather, and Pip's crossed-out arrows. "Lay them together," says Seren, "and they will show where the song leads." Where will you start?

bearing_notes.narration: You lay Pip's notebook over the chalk slate. The keeper checks each crossed-out arrow against her chalk lines. They all lean one way.

bearing_air.narration: You ring the edge with feathers and lanterns and call out. The keeper calls each direction back, so everyone can check it.

bearing_chime.narration: You ring the chime beside the song. Seren listens with you and points where its answering note leans.

bearing_sing.narration: Your songkeeper answers the low song. Seren waits for the echo while friends chalk its direction on the slate.

bearing_found.narration: Every clue points one way: east, past the dark edge, where the sky is singing. The keeper smiles for the first time since you landed. "The old keepers said cloud whales sing where the sky is safe to cross. If their song has moved, they may need help. Someone must go and see."

route_vote.narration: Dawn is a pale stripe. The keeper presses a flag-cloth with her island's mark into your hands. "Someone must see what is wrong with the singing. Thimble's ferry can take you part of the way. Fenwick can lead you along the stepping islands." How will you go?

route_ferry.narration: Thimble hands out boarding ropes. "Hold the rail, and no singing back until I say." Her passengers vote to stay with the keeper, hens and all, in case there is more tea. Dob loads his kite cart aboard and sits on top, map the right way up.

route_flags.narration: Fenwick clips three tiny flags to his wing. "I fly ahead and wave. If I wave two, hold on to something." A hen watches, deeply unimpressed. Dob will wait for the ferry, selling kites to anyone brave enough to look up.

island_done.narration: Dawn. The island falls away behind you, small and gold-roofed, its signal basket still glowing. Far off, a huge shape moves through the mist, singing. You have neighbors who trust you, a bearing, and a road to follow.

variants.text: The ferry hums under your feet.
Captain Thimble waves her string-tied hat. "You cannot miss the washing!" she calls.

gust_lull.narration: The open pad lies between you and the pole, and the wind comes in gusts. When a gust ends, every wind banner droops. "Wait for the lull," says the keeper, "then cross."

interaction.cue: Wait until the banners droop, then run to the pole.

onSuccess.narration: The banners droop, and you cross in one long stride.

onFailure.narration: A gust spins you twice and sits you down. The keeper reels you in on her rope.

onAssisted.narration: The keeper calls the lull. "Now!" You cross together without a stumble.

fuel_chain.narration: The fuel must go up the ladder to the basket. The keeper stands at the bottom, and Pip waits at the top, arms out like a very small harbor. "Hand to hand," calls the keeper, "and do not drop one on me."

interaction.cue: Catch the logs and pass them up the line.

onSuccess.narration: Pip drops the last log in with a clunk and a cheer. Nobody is hit. A miracle.

onFailure.narration: One log escapes and rolls under the shrine. The keeper fetches it, grumbling, and the basket fills anyway.

onAssisted.narration: The keeper hauls the last logs up on a rope. "A little help is still help," she says.

camp_play.narration: "What would make a good camp tonight?" asks the keeper. Pip suggests more hens. The hens suggest more barley.

interaction.cue: Add something to your cozy camp.

options.label: Hang a kite as a lantern shade
options.reaction: The kite glows like a paper moon, and the wind banners all lean in to look.

options.label: Pour hot barley tea
options.reaction: Steam curls up in the lantern light. A hen leans in for the smell.

options.label: Spread a thick blanket
options.reaction: The blanket fills with wind for a moment, then settles like a sleepy cat.

options.label: Tell a short, funny story
options.reaction: Pip laughs so hard he knocks his own pencil into the fire pit. It is rescued, slightly toasted.

onSuccess.narration: The camp glows. For one quiet minute, the island does not feel lost at all.

onFailure.narration: The camp is a little lopsided, with hens in the middle. It is perfect anyway.

onAssisted.narration: The keeper adds the last touches, humming. The camp is cozy before you know it.

song_track.narration: The song lights a glow in one of three wind-bells on the shrine. The glow hops from bell to bell like a flea. "Where it stops," says Seren, "is the way the song leads."

interaction.cue: Watch the glow hop between the bells, then pick where it ends.

onSuccess.narration: The glow settles in the east bell, humming. East.

onFailure.narration: You pick the wrong bell, and the east bell rings out cheerfully by itself. East, then.

onAssisted.narration: Seren points at the east bell. "There. Now you know what to prove."

song_echo.narration: The song comes again, close now, in a pattern: low, high, low, middle. "That is how whales say here we are," says Thimble. "Answer the same way," says Seren, "so they know a friend is listening."

interaction.cue: Watch the pattern, then ring it back on the bell.

onSuccess.narration: The song stops. Then one long, warm note answers from the east. "They heard us," says Seren.

onFailure.narration: Your pattern wobbles, but the song answers anyway, patient as a grown-up.

onAssisted.narration: Seren rings along and steadies each note. The song answers, long and warm.

wisps.narration: The bright basket draws little floating lights out of the dusk. Two wisps tumble in on the gale and circle the flame, giggling. They think it is a very large, very rude candle, and they want it. "They will pull it apart!" cries the keeper. "Shoo them off, gently!"

wisp_fight.narration: The wisps zip around the pole and dive at the flame. Drive them off before they tug the fire apart.

wisps_shooed.narration: The wisps squeak and bob away over the edge, still giggling. Pip scoops a spoonful of their leftover glow into a jar and screws on the lid. "For emergencies," he says, and hands it to you. "Or snacks." The keeper laughs so hard her ears flap.

wisps_rescued.narration: The wisps swirl until the world is all dizzy sparkles. The keeper rings the shrine bell with both paws. Wisps hate an honest bell, and they scatter with a rude little pop. The basket still burns, a little singed and very proud.

island_rest.narration: The ferry creaks at the pad, and Fenwick stretches in the first light. Beside the pad stands a stone hut. Its door rattles in the wind. Thump. Something soft hits the wall inside. Far off, the cloud whales sing.

dojo.narration: A bigfoot named Master Dunnick pulls you in out of the wind and leans on the door. The wind pushes. He pushes back. He has done this for forty years. "This school is called the Dojo. Here we train the Thornguard, a hero who holds the line." A thorn bracer hangs by the fire. A Thornguard's strength lives in it, and a song bell worn beside it will not ring. Thump. Students catch pillows falling from the rafters. "Anyone may try the bracer on."

variants.text: Master Dunnick is still leaning on the Dojo door. "Back already? Good." The thorn bracer waits on its hook. Thump. Another pillow drops.

dojo_pillows.narration: A student unties a rope, and pillows tumble from the rafters. You plant your feet and catch one, then another. The next lands on your head. "That is how you brace," says Master Dunnick. "Stand still, and let it come."

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
